newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Peru, Ecuador meet to begin border dispute talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru, Ecuador meet to begin border dispute talks.

text.p: Officials from Ecuador and Peru met in Brazil on Tuesday to begin negotiating a settlement to a long-running border dispute that boiled over into a short war in 1995.

Ecuadorean foreign minister Jose Ayala Lazo and his interim counterpart from Peru, Jorge Gonzalez Izquierdo, said they were confident of progressing toward a solution for their rival claims to the Cordillera del Condor region.

"We have reached full understanding on how to proceed (with the talks) so there has been an auspicious beginning," Ecuador's Ayala Lazo told reporters shortly before the talks were due to begin at Brazil's Foreign Ministry.

Peru's Gonzalez Izquierdo, replacing foreign minister Francisco Tudela who is being held captive by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement guerrillas in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, also sounded upbeat.
"We hope we can reach agreement quickly over most of the impasses," Izquierdo said.
Dozens of soldiers from both countries were killed in a month-long war 1995, the latest in a string of clashes between Peru and Ecuador over the 130 square-mile (340 square km) zone.
The United States welcomed the talks between the countries as a means of consummating "peace in our hemisphere."

"The United States welcomes the April 15 opening of the first stage of substantive border talks between Ecuador and Peru and congratulates the two countries for their determination to consummate peace in our hemisphere," said a White House statement, issued in New York on a visit by U.S. President Bill Clinton to the city.
